files.lesson.md: --- order: 29 unit: solids9 node: AC9M9M01 n2 uses: [AC9M9M01 n1, AC9M8M03 n1] assumes: [AC9M9M01 n1] connection: rainwater-tank title: Volume of prisms and cylinders summary: "A prism or a cylinder is the same layer, stacked. Its volume is the area of the base times the height: V = Ah, and for a cylinder V = πr²h." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How much water does a round rainwater tank hold?" --- Rain falling on a roof runs into a tank. The Bureau of Meteorology says each millimetre of rain on each square metre gives about a litre ([Bureau of Meteorology](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/how/faq-data.shtml), checked 25 October 2026). A tank is a cylinder with a radius of 1.1 m and a height of 2 m (made up for the task). How many litres can it hold? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: how much it holds ```step stage: predict insight: "Estimating the tank's volume shows whether students use the diameter, the radius or a full-size box." check: type: predict q: "A tank is a cylinder with radius 1.1 m and height 2 m. About how many cubic metres does it hold?" options: - "About 7.6 m³" - "About 4.4 m³" - "About 2.4 m³" - "About 15 m³" actual: "About 7.6 m³. The base is a circle of area π × 1.1² ≈ 3.8 m², and the tank is 2 m tall. A box 2.2 m wide each way would hold 9.7 m³, a bit more than the round tank." ``` ## Run: layers ```step stage: run insight: "Stacking layers of equal area gives V = base area × height." check: { type: number, q: "The base of the tank is a circle of radius $1.1$ m. What is its area? (use $\\pi \\approx 3.14$; m², 2 decimal places)", answer: 3.8, tolerance: 0.02, explain: "3.14 × 1.1 × 1.1 = 3.80 m²." } ``` ## Investigate: base times height ```step stage: investigate insight: "Volume is the base area times the height for any prism or cylinder, and the base's area depends on the radius, not the diameter." tasks: - check: type: number q: "The base area is $3.8$ m² and the tank is $2$ m tall. What is its volume? (m³, 1 decimal place)" answer: 7.6 tolerance: 0.1 explain: "3.8 × 2 = 7.6 m³." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $3.8 \\times 2$?", answer: 7.6, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "3.8 × 2 = 7.6." } - check: type: number q: "$1$ m³ is $1000$ litres. How many litres does the tank hold? (to the nearest 100)" answer: 7600 tolerance: 50 explain: "7.6 × 1000 = 7600 L." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#raj" text: "Raj finds the volume of a tank with diameter 2.2 m and height 2 m. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: diameter-as-radius explain: "Line 3: 2.2 m is the diameter. The formula needs the radius, which is 1.1 m." ``` ### Base times height ```worked V = A \times h :: Volume: base area times height. A = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 1.1^2 = 3.8 :: The base is a circle. V = 3.8 \times 2 = 7.6 \text{ m}^3 :: The cylinder's volume. 7.6 \times 1000 = 7600 \text{ L} :: 1 m³ = 1000 litres. ``` ### Base area ### Find the mistake Read Raj's working. Which line uses the diameter for the radius? ## Modify: other prisms ```step stage: modify insight: "The same V = Ah works for any prism; only the base changes." tasks: - hint: ["The base is a triangle.", "½ × 6 × 4 = 12, then × 10."] check: { type: number, q: "A triangular prism has a triangular base with base $6$ and height $4$ (cm) and the prism is $10$ cm long. What is its volume? (cm³)", answer: 120, explain: "Base area ½ × 6 × 4 = 12, volume 12 × 10 = 120 cm³." } - hint: ["Radius is half the diameter.", "r = 1.5."] check: { type: number, q: "A cylinder has diameter $3$ cm and height $10$ cm. What is its volume? (cm³, nearest whole number, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)", answer: 71, tolerance: 1, explain: "r = 1.5, so 3.14 × 1.5² × 10 = 70.65, about 71 cm³." } - hint: ["1 m³ = 1000 L.", "Use the volume you've found."] check: { type: question, q: "A tank holds $7.6$ m³. A roof of $100$ m² gets $76$ mm of rain, which gives $76 \\times 100 = 7600$ L. Does the tank fill, and is the result exact?", options: ["It just fills in theory, but real roofs lose some water, so it is approximate", "It overflows", "It is exactly full", "It can't be calculated"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "7600 L is the tank's capacity, so no overflow.", "The BoM calls the figure approximate.", "It can be estimated."], explain: "1 mm of rain on 1 m² is about a litre (approximate). Some water is lost, so the tank is likely a little under full." } ``` ### A triangular prism ### Diameter to radius ### Does the tank fill ## Practise: volume ```step stage: practise insight: "Base area times height for prisms and cylinders, with units." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A box has base 4 cm by 5 cm and height 6 cm. What is its volume? (cm³)" answer: 120 explain: "4 × 5 × 6 = 120." - check: type: number q: "A cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 5 cm. What is its volume? (cm³, 1 decimal place, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" answer: 62.8 tolerance: 0.2 explain: "3.14 × 4 × 5 = 62.8." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is the area of the base, radius 2 cm? (use 3.14; cm²)", answer: 12.6, tolerance: 0.1, explain: "3.14 × 2 × 2 = 12.56." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a can has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. What is its curved surface area? (cm², nearest whole number)" answer: 188 tolerance: 1 explain: "2 × 3.14 × 3 × 10 = 188.4." ``` ### Box ### Cylinder ### Review ## Make: the tank ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the tank: work out the capacity in litres and compare with a rainfall." tasks: - hint: ["Base area × height.", "Then × 1000 to get litres."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The tank has radius 1.1 m and height 2 m (made up for the task). How many litres can it hold? (nearest 100, $\\pi \\approx 3.14$)" steps: - ["$A = 3.14 \\times 1.1^2 = 3.8$", "the base area in m²"] - ["$V = 3.8 \\times 2 = 7.6$", "volume in m³"] - ["$7.6 \\times 1000 = 7600$", "litres"] answer: "7600" answerLabel: "Capacity (litres)" tolerance: 100 feedback: - ["7.6", "That's cubic metres. Multiply by 1000 for litres."] - ["2.4", "That uses the diameter somewhere: check the radius."] criteria: - "I used the radius, not the diameter." - "I multiplied the base area by the height." - "I converted to litres." explain: "7.6 m³ is about 7600 L." - check: type: question q: "A roof of 80 m² catches 50 mm of rain. About how many litres is that?" options: ["About 4000 L", "About 130 L", "About 400 L", "About 40,000 L"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That adds instead of multiplying.", "Each mm on each m² is about a litre: 80 × 50.", "That has a zero too many."] explain: "80 × 50 = 4000 L (approximate, as the Bureau says)." ``` ### Capacity ### Rain on a roof **Also used in** - **Water and storage.** Tanks, pipes, silos and bottles are cylinders. - **Cooking.** A tin's contents in millilitres: 1 cm³ is 1 mL. - **Next lesson.** Problems that use surface area and volume together. ```teacher summary: Students find the volume of prisms and cylinders as base area times height (AC9M9M01, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can use V = Ah for a prism. - I can use V = πr²h for a cylinder. - I can change cubic metres into litres. struggle: "Using the diameter. Ask: is that the full way across or half way?" before: > Students need Surface area from nets. The one idea: stack the base layer. For a cylinder the base is a circle, so use the radius. 1 mm of rain on 1 m² is about 1 litre (Bureau of Meteorology: approximate). The tank and roof sizes are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the tank in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student gets about 30 m³ for the tank. ask: Is 2.2 the radius? fix: "It's the diameter: halve it." stretch: How tall would a tank of the same radius need to be to hold 10,000 L? support: A printed layer picture with the base shaded. leads: | Continues AC9M9M01 node 2. Where it leads: Problems with surface area and volume. exit: q: A cylinder has radius 2 and height 5. What is the base area times the height? a: π × 4 × 5 ≈ 62.8. explain: | A prism or cylinder is a base layer stacked up to the height: V = Ah. For a cylinder A = πr², so V = πr²h. ```
